We’re looking for a Swedish Account Executive/Manager to join our team. We’re seeing strong momentum in demand for our eID (electronic identity) solutions, and there’s a big opportunity to help organizations integrate secure logins and digital signatures using eIDs.

About Idura

We help organizations securely verify users and support digital signing through eID integrations. As an official MitID broker in Denmark, we also support additional European eIDs, including BankID, FTN, and more. Our solutions are KYC-compliant, user-friendly, and aligned with standards such as PAdES and eIDAS.

In September 2024, Idura was acquired by Stø (formerly BankID BankAxept), strengthening Stø’s position in European digital identity. Stø is owned by the banks in Norway through the company Vipps Holding AS.

About the role

• 
Employment: Full-time.

• 
Location: Copenhagen office (or remote from Sweden)

• 
You’ll manage the full sales cycle, from prospecting and qualifying to presenting solutions, negotiating, and closing.

• 
Expect a mix of inbound and outbound leads, plus upselling to existing customers.

• 
You’ll work closely with Marketing, Product, and Technical teams to support onboarding, implementation, and customer success.

• 
You’ll maintain your pipeline and reporting in HubSpot CRM.

You’ll report to VP Sales Lars Mørch and be part of an international sales team.

What you’ll bring

• 
3+ years of proven B2B sales experience, ideally in SaaS, cybersecurity, or identity management.

• 
Strong pipeline-building, solution-selling, and closing skills.

• 
The ability to explain technical topics clearly, including authentication, digital signatures, APIs, and integrations.

• 
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills across business and technical teams.

• 
Fluency in Swedish and strong English skills.

• 
CRM proficiency (HubSpot/Salesforce) and a structured approach to forecasting and reporting.

• 
Experience in regulated or KYC-focused environments is a bonus.

Application process

We’ll review applications throughout November and begin interviews in early December.

Application deadline: November 30.

For more information or questions please contact us at albert@thehub.io

Idura is a Copenhagen-based company specializing in secure user authentication and digital signature solutions using electronic identities (eIDs). We empower companies to integrate eIDs into websites or applications effortlessly, ensuring an efficient, secure login or signature process at a cost-effective price. As an official MitID broker in Denmark, we offer MitID as well as a range of European eIDs, including BankID in Sweden and Norway, Finnish Trust Network (FTN) and itsme in Belgium. Our mission is to ensure the highest level of security in digital verification, making the digital world a safer place to roam. Authentication We provide a fast and simple integration of eIDs for businesses that want to verify their customers on their website or app. Our solution allows your users to authenticate themselves with secure and KYC compliant eIDs, which provides the most secure and user-friendly login experience possible. Digital signatures Implement digital signatures into your workflow and sign PDF documents digitally with eIDs. We ensure that all of our digital signatures are secure and compliant with PAdES and eIDAS.

Tenure-track Assistant Professor, Associate Professor or Full Professor of Food Processing & Technology
 Department of Food Science
 Faculty of Science
 University of Copenhagen

  The Department of Food Science, Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen invites applications for a position as Tenure-track Assistant Professor, Associate Professor or Full Professor in Food Processing and Technology. Applicants must be capable of, and interested in, conducting and developing basic and applied interdisciplinary research of high international standard in the field of food processing and technology. The position will involve extensive collaborations within the department and with national and international academic groups and industrial partners. Research within the Department has a mission to unearth new solutions for society and industry to support sustainable food production, food security and safety as well as production of high-quality food promoting human health and wellbeing. The Department of Food Science is recognized for excellence in food research, education, and industrial collaborations. The Department is an international workplace with Danish and English as parallel working languages, however it is expected that the successful candidate will be able to contribute to teaching in Danish within 3 to 6 years. We encourage applications from a range of disciplines within the food science and technology area, ideally covering the understanding of food macromolecular interactions on a mechanistic level, how processing and formulation affect or determine these interactions, and how this influences final product quality with focus on functional properties.

  We are seeking a candidate who will establish an internationally leading research program, and we encourage a diverse range of applicants whose work may center on one or more of the following disciplines:

   	
• Developing a mechanistic understanding of interactions of food macromolecules in complex matrices during processing or formulation spanning dairy, plant, and single-cell protein sources. 	
• How this knowledge can be used in the rational design of functional ingredients and healthy foods using established and emerging processing technologies 	
• Development and utilization of high throughput methods for characterizing and quantifying the physicochemical behavior of food macromolecules in complex matrices. 	
• Modelling and the use of machine learning/AI for simulation and prediction of the outcome of process unit operations on food and ingredient functionality. 	
• Formulation and fluid dynamics of complex emulsions and the mechanisms governing this.   In addition, it is expected that this position will be involved in a significant amount of collaboration with industry, and therefore it is expected that the successful candidate has a documented successful track record in industry collaboration and working with innovation-oriented research. Furthermore, we expect that the successful candidate has a genuine interest in leadership and the wellbeing and development of their group.

  Tenure-track assistant professor
 The tenure-track assistant professor’s duties will primarily include research, including obligations with regards to publication/scientific communication and research-based teaching with associated examination obligations within the Tenure Track Assistant Professorship. To a limited extent the position may also include other duties.

  The tenure-track assistant professor must have an academic standing showing internationally competitive research, and/or have internationally recognized high potential to make a future impact.

  Assessment of applicants for the tenure-track assistant professorship will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory but documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered.

  Associate professor and full professor

  Applicants are required to have university level teaching experience, documented teaching competencies and must be able to explain and reflect upon own teaching practice and portfolio. Formal pedagogical training or supervision equivalent to the University of Copenhagen teacher training programme for assistant professors is required.
 In particular, the candidate must actively contribute with research-based teaching on the BSc in Food Science and Nutrition, and the MSc in Food Science and Technology programs, with an emphasis on the specialization in Dairy Science and Technology.

  Duties include the applicant’s own research, development of the field, assessment tasks, grant applications, and research management such as supervision and training of research fellows and other staff. The successful applicant must also teach, supervise, prepare and participate in examinations, and fulfill other tasks requested by the Department.

  Assessment of applicants for the associate professorship and full professorship will primarily consider their level of documented, original scientific production at an international level, including contributions to developments in their field, as well as their documented teaching qualifications. Managerial and out-reach qualifications of applicants including ability to attract external funding will also be considered.

  University of Copenhagen’s criteria for recognising merit
 General criteria apply to the appointment of assistant professor / associate professor / professor at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, Innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

  Please read more here:
 
 For tenure-track assistant professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5a_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-Assistant_professors.pdf

  For associate professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5b_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-Associate_professors.pdf

  For professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5c_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-professors.pdf

  Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen's Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact here

  The tenure-track assistant programme
 The tenure-track programme is a career programme and an assigned mentor will provide the tenure-track assistant professors with guidance related to career development, other academic topics and administrative procedures.

  Performance of the tenure-track assistant professor will be followed via internal yearly evaluations and a mid-term and final international evaluation by an assessment committee. If the ‘final appraisal’ is positive you will be promoted as associate professor. Performance and progression towards the criteria below will be evaluated with due consideration of differences between research fields.

  After a 6-year tenure-track period tenure-track assistant professors are expected to meet the criteria for appointment of associate professors at the University of Copenhagen.

  Salary and employment conditions
 The position is open from 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Employment is either as tenure track assistant professor, associate professor or professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  This position comes with an opportunity to negotiate a start package that will help leverage the candidate’s scientific deliverables in the initial years of employment. The negotiation for the start package takes place as part of the recruitment process. Please read about the contents of the programme and conditions, as well as UCPH’s extensive support for international researchers, here Start package programme – University of Copenhagen .  

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  The successful candidate will be a part of the Section for Ingredients and Dairy Technology. The section has internationally acknowledged expertise within novel sustainable processing technologies, protein, polyphenol and lipid chemistry, functionality, and modification of food components, kinetics, oxidation, food engineering, rheology, digitalisation, and advanced data analysis. The section is also equipped with pilot facilities for brewing, dairy and bioprocessing. The section has extensive collaborations on research projects with major food industries in both Denmark and abroad.

  Further information on the Department is linked at Department of Food Science – University of Copenhagen Inquiries about the position can be made to Inquiries about the position can be made to Head of Department, Colin Ray (+45 93565911, colin.ray@food.ku.dk) or Head of Section, Mogens Larsen Andersen (+45 3533 3262, mola@food.ku.dk).

  Filing of application
 The position may be applied for at the tenure-track assistant professor level, associate professor level or full professor level. Please note that it is possible to apply at more than one level. If applied at more than one level, separate applications must be submitted (see below).

  The application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. 

  Applying for the tenure-track assistant professorship please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae including: 	 		
• Please describe and document international network and relations 		
• Please describe and document internationally based activities 		
• Positions held at universities/research institutions outside Denmark 		
• Outreach activities, i.e. popular lectures or other activities in the media 		
• Grants held, personal or in part. Career development grants. 	 	 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent)    	
• Research plan - description of current and future research plans    	
• If available, description and documentation of teaching and supervision experience and qualifications- please describe and document: 	 		
• Experience with supervision of BSc and MSc students 		
• Teaching experience 		
• Formal pedagogical training 	 	    	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of up to 5 particularly relevant papers   Applying for the associate professorship or full professorship please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae including information about external funding  	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent)  	
• Research plan – description of current and future research plans  	
• Description and documentation of teaching experience and qualifications according to university guidelines 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 5 particularly relevant papers   The deadline for applications is 3 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. 

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Interviews will be held on 25 February 2027.  

  Please refer to the following no. in future communication in this case: 

  211-0262/26-2N, Tenure-track Assistant Professor of Food Processing & Technology.

  211-0759/26-2E, Associate Professor of Food Processing & Technology. 

  211-0366/26-2K, Professor of Food Processing & Technology.

Are you interested in sustainability, enjoy working with data, and want to turn reporting requirements into practical action? Join Flatpay and help build the foundations of our ESG work across our seven European markets and the US!

We’re looking for a curious, structured colleague who enjoys digging into details, connecting with people, and bringing order to complex information.

About Flatpay

Flatpay is not just another payment solution; we're dedicated to innovating the market for payment solutions and financial services in the SME segment with our customer-centric and transparent services.

We've grown into one of the fastest-growing fintech companies out of the Nordics and Denmark's fastest unicorn company. Today, we're more than 2,500 colleagues across Europe and the US, building products that make a real difference for our customers.

We're ambitious, move fast, and like to challenge the status quo - but we also believe work should be fun. We celebrate wins, help each other out, and create an environment where people can do great work while genuinely enjoying the journey.

What you'll do

You’ll coordinate ESG data collection and reporting across our markets, working with internal teams, suppliers, and external compliance partners. From reviewing supplier documentation to improving reporting processes, you’ll help ensure we have reliable information and clear ways of working as we grow.

This is a hands-on role with international exposure and room to develop. You’ll help shape Flatpay’s ESG function from the ground up, taking increasing ownership as your knowledge and experience grow.

• 
Coordinate ESG reporting across markets. Organize data collection, follow up on inputs, and support accurate, timely reporting, including CSRD-related work where applicable.

• 
Build a reliable data foundation. Review compliance reports, product documentation, and supplier data sheets; identify gaps; and source the information needed for reporting.

• 
Work across teams and borders. Collaborate with colleagues, suppliers, and external compliance partners to make reporting processes clear and manageable.

• 
Track relevant requirements. Help assess what developments in CSRD, the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR), and local producer responsibility schemes mean for Flatpay.

• 
Coordinate producer responsibility reporting. Work with Dansk Producentansvar (DPA), equivalent organisations in other markets, and relevant compliance partners.

• 
Support practical sustainability initiatives. Contribute to improvements in reverse logistics, refurbishment, and how we manage products throughout their lifecycle.

• 
Help establish our ESG function. Build processes, improve data quality, and gradually become an internal point of contact for sustainability reporting and compliance questions.

Who you are

• 
An interest in ESG and sustainability, particularly the data and reporting behind them.

• 
An analytical mindset and confidence working with spreadsheets and structured data.

• 
A careful, organised approach: you spot inconsistencies, ask questions, and follow through.

• 
The ability to work with colleagues and suppliers to get the information you need.

• 
Curiosity about regulations and the ability to translate complex information into clear next steps.

• 
Strong communication skills in English and an interest in working across international markets.

Previous exposure to ESG reporting, sustainability, compliance, or data analysis is a plus. This could come from a full-time role, student position or involvement in relevant project. Familiarity with CSRD or producer responsibility is welcome, but you don’t need to arrive as an expert in every framework.

Why Flatpay

Joining Flatpay means stepping into a dynamic environment where innovation is encouraged, and teamwork is celebrated. Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, contributing to our mission of empowering merchants to succeed.

In this role, you'll have the opportunity to build practical ESG experience across multiple markets and see the direct impact of your work. Your ideas will help shape our processes, strengthen our reporting, and inform how we approach sustainability as we scale.

With us, you’ll experience an ambitious drive to constantly push boundaries and redefine what's possible. While we don’t take ourselves too seriously, we take our responsibility towards our people very seriously. We welcome driven, low-ego individuals who live our values and want to grow with us.

WHAT IS FLATPAY? At Flatpay, we believe that merchants deserve a payment solution that is easy to understand, affordable, and free from hidden fees. That's why we offer a straightforward pricing model with no setup fees for terminals, no subscription fees, and a flat rate for all card types. It's a breath of fresh air compared to the complicated and confusing pricing structures of our competitors.  What sets Flatpay apart is our dedication. We continuously strive to stay ahead of the curve, adapting our solutions to meet our client's evolving needs. Ready to be part of something extraordinary? WHAT's THE CULTURE LIKE? Flatpay is a fast-moving, performance-driven environment where people are trusted to take ownership from day one. We value initiative, resilience, and a strong work ethic. Our teams are collaborative and supportive, but we also set clear expectations and hold ourselves accountable to results.  As a growing business, things move quickly. That means you’ll have the opportunity to take on real responsibility early, contribute ideas, and see the impact of your work directly. It also means being comfortable with change, solving problems as they arise, and continuously improving how we operate.  We’re best suited to people who are motivated by challenge, enjoy working towards clear goals, and want to develop in a commercial, high-energy environment. WHY CHOOSE FLATPAY? Flatpay offers the opportunity to take real ownership, develop valuable skills, and grow your career in a fast-moving, ambitious company where performance and initiative are recognised.

ABOUT THE JOB

Flatpay is on a mission to simplify payments for small and medium-sized businesses. We provide transparent, low-cost payment solutions combined with fast onboarding and real human support - fair pricing, great technology, and local support that merchants can rely on. One of the fastest-growing fintech companies out of the Nordics and Denmark's fastest-ever unicorn, we've scaled to 2,500+ colleagues across multiple markets, and we're just getting started. Pay is our terminal-only product: a card terminal, flat transparent pricing, and nothing the merchant has to configure. It is the product most of our merchants gets first, it carries the majority of our processing volume, and it is the product we lead with in every new market. This is a deliberately commercial product leadership role. Flatpay's whole model rests on a single visit: a rep walks into a bakery, a salon or a bike shop unannounced, explains flat, transparent pricing, demos the terminal, installs it and trains the staff. Everything Pay does exists to make that visit convert and to keep the merchant on the terminal afterwards. If you've only ever led product through a research team and a dashboard, this won't be the role for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own Pay end to end

• 
Own the Pay product globally - terminal hardware, the payment experience, onboarding and activation, the merchant app, settlement and reporting. One roadmap, all markets.

• 
Set the Pay strategy and defend it: what we build, what we deliberately do not build, and what stays the same across every market so the product does not fragment as we add countries.

• 
Keep the product radically simple. Our merchants are not technical and have no IT function; simplicity is the product, and protecting it is your job before it is anyone else's.

Lead the team

• 
Lead and grow the Pay product team (three PMs today, with the reporting track dotted in), setting the bar for discovery, delivery and written thinking.

• 
Be a player-coach. You'll run your own track on the hardest problems, not only review other people's.

• 
Partner with Engineering, Design and Data in Copenhagen to turn the Pay roadmap into shipped product on roughly two-month cycles, MVP mindset - get it live, learn, iterate.

The field

• 
Get out into the field. Sit with merchants, ride along with sales, spend time with support, and turn what you hear into product decisions. We expect this of a Head of Pay as much as of a PM.

• 
Partner with Sales, Support and Marketing across markets to surface what is actually happening with merchants, and feed it straight into the roadmap.

• 
Build and hold the competitive view for Pay: how competitors package and price terminal and Pay-only offers in Europe and the US, and where they are beatable.

Markets and expansion

• 
Make Pay launch-ready for each new market - acquiring setup, local payment behaviour, regulation, hardware logistics - and work with the US team in New York on what the US needs from the European product.

• 
Own outcome metrics for Pay: activation, processing volume, retention, churn, support load, and the commercial metrics above.

WHO YOU ARE

• 
3+ years in product, with experience leading product managers - and still extremely hands-on.

• 
A commercial, results-driven mindset. You think in merchants, conversion, volume and margin, and you can point to a pricing or product decision you made that moved one of them.

• 
Evidence of field-driven discovery: a decision you can name that came directly from time in front of merchants or sales, not from a research readout.

• 
A track record of shipping fast in a low-structure environment, and comfort building the structure as you go rather than waiting for it.

• 
A generalist and builder who thrives in a fast-paced scale-up and is happy working outside their comfort zone.

• 
Excellent stakeholder management across functions, markets and time zones, and excellent written and spoken English.

AI IS PART OF THE JOB

• 
Flatpay's cost advantage comes from doing things with fewer people than the incumbents. AI is how we keep that true as we add markets, and we expect a Head of Pay to treat it as part of the product, not as a side project.

• 
Use it yourself, daily. You prototype with it, you write specs and analysis with it, you run your own competitive and pricing research with it. You'll be setting the bar for three PMs, and the bar is that a PM who cannot get a working prototype or a data answer in an afternoon is slower than the role now requires.

• 
Know where it does not belong. Nothing in the authorisation path, nothing the merchant has to supervise, nothing that makes a terminal less predictable. Our merchants are not technical and have no IT function.

• 
Be honest about the economics. Inference cost, error rate and the cost of being wrong are product decisions. You should be able to argue why a model belongs in a flow at our volumes, or why a rule set is the better answer.

WHY FLATPAY?

As part of our team, you will join +2000 passionate Flatpayers dedicated to shaping the future of payments in Europe. Flatpay is proud to be a company that values diversity. We ensure an inclusive work environment for all our employees and offer opportunities for professional growth and development. We have free slushice, an on-site gym, a fully equipped gamer room, and plenty of other fun things at our office! If you are ready to be part of this exciting journey, we would love to hear from you today.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

The role

You'll be the person who takes a video from idea to finished file — on your own.

Say we need a product walkthrough of a new Veo feature. Here's what that looks like for you:

• 
Plan: Set the shoot date and book the product designer who built the feature.

• 
Find the story: Interview them and write the script.

• 
Set up: Light and frame the set.

• 
Shoot: Run the shoot on our two Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 6Ks and direct the person on camera.

• 
Finish: Edit, grade, mix, subtitle, and export every format we need.

Nobody hands you a shot list. Nobody needs to check in halfway.

You'll also use AI throughout your work. Some shots you'll generate in tools like Higgsfield instead of filming them. Some steps — transcripts, rough cuts, subtitles, versioning — you'll hand to AI so you can spend your time on the parts that need your eye.

You'll join Veo's Owned & Creative team in Copenhagen, working alongside graphic designers, a video producer focused on AI-generated ads, and the wider marketing team.

What you'll do

Own production end-to-end

• 
Take a brief (or spot the need yourself) and turn it into a production plan: concept, timeline, locations, people, and gear.

• 
Plan and book shoot dates with colleagues across Veo, from product designers to coaches and community members.

• 
Research the topic and interview subject-matter experts to find the story worth telling.

• 
Write scripts, talking points, and storyboards.

Run the shoot

• 
Set up the set: lighting, sound, framing, and camera settings.

• 
Operate our 2× Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 6K setup, including multi-camera interviews and B-roll.

• 
Direct and interview people on camera — most of them aren't actors — so they come across confident and natural, and stick to the script when they need to.

• 
Shoot on location, in studio, and out on the pitch.

Finish the video

• 
Edit in DaVinci Resolve or Premiere Pro: story, pacing, color grading, sound mix, graphics, subtitles, and CTAs.

• 
Deliver multi-format versions for paid social (Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, Instagram), YouTube, veo.co, and email.

• 
Organize and archive footage and finished assets in our DAM (Frontify) so the whole team can find and reuse them.

Make AI part of how you work

• 
Generate shots, B-roll, and scenes with AI video tools such as Higgsfield, and blend them with live-action footage.

• 
Use AI to speed up your workflow — automated transcripts and rough cuts, text-based editing, AI subtitles, script drafts, and fast versioning for different markets and formats.

• 
Keep testing new tools and share what works with the team.

Work with the team — without needing to be managed

• 
Align with graphic designers on art direction and brand, and with marketers on campaign goals.

• 
Manage your own pipeline, priorities, and deadlines, and flag trade-offs early.

• 
Brief and coordinate freelancers (photographers, extra crew) when a project needs them.

What we're looking for

• 
A portfolio that shows videos you've taken from idea to final cut — ideally including interview-led or product content. Please tell us what you did on each piece.

• 
3+ years of hands-on video production experience, in-house, at an agency, or freelance.

• 
Strong camera skills — confident with cinema cameras (Blackmagic experience is a plus), lighting, and recording clean audio.

• 
Strong editing skills in DaVinci Resolve or Premiere Pro, including color grading and sound. After Effects or motion graphics experience is a plus.

• 
You can direct people. You know how to make a nervous colleague relaxed on camera and how to interview to get a good answer.

• 
You write. You can turn an interview or a product brief into a clear script.

• 
You already use AI in your work — or you're curious and actively learning. Experience with AI video generation (e.g. Higgsfield, Runway, Kling, Veo, Sora) and AI-assisted editing is a strong plus.

• 
You're proactive and independent. You see what needs doing, make the call, and get it done. You're comfortable working without close supervision and owning the outcome.

• 
You understand performance content — what makes a viewer stop scrolling and how formats differ by channel.

• 
Fluent in English. Danish is a plus.

• 
Based in the Greater Copenhagen area.

Additional information

Before inviting candidates to interviews, we'll ask you to complete a small task. We'll only use it for the recruitment process, never commercially.

How to apply

• 
Attach your CV and a short cover letter. Tell us about a video you owned from start to finish, and how you use AI in your workflow.

• 
Include a link to your portfolio.

• 
Complete the application form.

Life at Veo

We're an office-first company. Our Copenhagen office has an indoor ball court, a rooftop terrace, and a well-equipped gym. It's built to connect people across the business, spark creative thinking, and give you space to work with colleagues, global partners, and the wider Veo community.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Positions in Experimental Nanophotonics and Quantum Optics
jobs.description:
The research group of Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen at the Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for two Postdoctoral Researcher positions in experimental nanophotonics and quantum optics.

  Professor Mikkelsen’s group studies how light and matter interact when light is confined to nanometre-scale volumes. Using plasmonic nanocavities — metallic nanogaps fabricated deterministically around a chosen emitter — the group reaches a regime far beyond the reach of conventional optical cavities: Purcell factors above 10,000, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths with lifetimes of tens of picoseconds at room temperature, and second-harmonic generation enhanced more than ten-million-fold in materials with no bulk nonlinearity. In this regime, light–matter behaviour appears that was not previously thought possible, and the group’s experiments are increasingly directed at the nonlinear and ultrafast optics it opens up. Experiments combine nanofabrication, single-photon and photon-correlation spectroscopy, cryogenic magneto-optics and ultrafast pump–probe optics. The group has recently relocated from Duke University to NBI, supported by a DKK 35 million RECRUIT award from the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and is establishing a laboratory in NBI’s new building. Postdocs joining now will help build the laboratory and shape its first experiments. Recent work: https://mikkelsenphotonics.com.

  The positions span three axes of control over light–matter interaction; the balance between them will depend on the candidates:

  Spatial structure — shaping the vacuum around an emitter and concentrating the field for nonlinear optics, with examples including Purcell tensors, the nanophotonic Lamb shift, harmonic generation in nanoscale volumes, and forbidden and two-photon transitions opened by field gradients.

  Emitter number — cavity QED with exactly one, two or several emitters, including the crossover from room-temperature to cryogenic strong coupling, collective emission, and multi-exciton emission that outruns Auger recombination.

  Temporal control — ultrafast and time-resolved experiments on single nanocavities, including single-nanocavity pump–probe spectroscopy, optically dressed states in quantum materials embedded in nanogaps, and time-varying cavities.

  We seek outstanding, creative, and highly motivated experimentalists with a PhD in physics, chemistry, materials science, electrical engineering, or a closely related discipline, and a strong background in one or more of: nanophotonics or cavity QED; quantum optics and photon-correlation measurements; cryogenic spectroscopy of solid-state emitters or two-dimensional materials; ultrafast optical spectroscopy; nanofabrication. Candidates are encouraged to propose directions of their own within this scope; the programme will be shaped by the people who join.

  The successful candidates will carry out experimental research, help set up the new laboratory, including a 1.7 K cryostat with a vector magnet, a tunable femtosecond laser system and single-photon confocal spectroscopy, publish and present results, and participate in the supervision of students. The positions may also include collaboration with national and international research partners and other academic duties as required. The group fabricates its cavities in the NBI cleanroom and at DTU Nanolab, Denmark's national nanofabrication centre.

   

  Further information on the Department at https://nbi.ku.dk/english/. Informal inquiries are welcome and can be made to Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen, maiken.mikkelsen@nbi.ku.dk.

  The positions are for three years, starting as soon as possible, with flexible start dates into 2027.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff. 

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. 

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. 

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Please include 

   	
• Cover letter describing your motivation and research interests (max 1 page) 	
• Curriculum vitae, including publication list 	
• Diplomas (Master’s and PhD degree, or documentation of expected PhD completion date) 	
• Names and contact details of two or three references   The deadline for applications is 1 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee.
